title: GPUParticles2D are invisible when process material collision mode is enabled
body:
### Tested versions

Godot v4.5.1.stable

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - AMD Ryzen 9 7950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 63.14 GiB memory

### Issue description

GPUParticles2D are invisible when process material collision mode is enabled (Rigid or Hide on Contact).
This happens consistently when editing the scene containing the GPUParticles2D.

In the game I am working on, when I switch over to a parent scene containing the particles, they become visible again, even though collision is still enabled. However in the testing I did the particles were invisible even in the parent scene, and when running the project.

Interestingly, by moving the console output window up and down, you can actually see the particles moving again. But they disappear as soon as you stop jiggling the window.


### Steps to reproduce

GPUParticles2D invisible in root scene:
- Create a new GPUParticles2D.
- Assign any texture.
- Assign a new ParticleProcessMaterial. (The particles should now be visible and falling.)
- Under Collision, change from Disabled to Rigid or Hide on Contact.
- Observe the particles disappear. (Change collision back to Disabled and they should re-appear.)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[gpu-particles-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23610746/gpu-particles-test.zip)
